weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.character: Small S3ApiServer helpers resolving the caller's account id for ACL and ownership decisions
gotchas: getAccountId trusts the s3-account-id header; it is only safe because iam.Auth deletes any client value and sets its own (authenticateRequestInternal defers r.Header.Del(AmzAccountId) and authRequestWithAuthType sets it).
weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.if_broken: Objects and buckets get the wrong owner, or non-owners can change ownership controls.
weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.ux: Owner ids shown in ACLs; AccessDenied for non-owners on ownership controls.
weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.what: getAccountId reads the s3-account-id header that auth sets (anonymous when absent); requestAccountId and ownerAccountId return the admin account when auth is disabled (the header is then client-supplied) and map anonymous to admin for ownership; checkAccessByOwnership allows the ownership-controls APIs only to admins or the bucket owner recorded in the BucketRegistry.
weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.when: ACL handlers, upload ACL preparation, PutBucket ACL parsing, ownership-controls handlers.
weed/s3api/s3api_acp.go.why: Consequence: ACL grants and bucket owner records are written with these ids, so trusting a client-supplied header would let anyone claim ownership. Design: with auth off there is no verified caller, so the admin account stands in; admin is detected by capability (isUserAdmin), not account id, because account-less identities share the 'admin' id. AWS compatibility: Get/Put/DeleteBucketOwnershipControls are owner-only.

weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.character: Stateless request classifiers: the authType enum and getRequestAuthType
gotchas: isRequestSignatureV2 matches any Authorization starting with 'AWS' that is not AWS4-HMAC-SHA256.
Streaming detection applies only to PUT; a POST with a streaming content-sha256 falls through to the header-based checks.
weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.if_broken: Valid signed requests are rejected or, worse, unsigned requests are processed as anonymous where anonymous access is granted.
weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.ux: Invisible; it determines whether presigned URLs, SDK streaming uploads, OIDC bearer tokens and anonymous public reads work.
weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.what: Classifies a request by the credential it carries: SigV2 header ('AWS ' prefix that is not AWS4), SigV2 presigned (?AWSAccessKeyId), streaming SigV4 PUT (x-amz-content-sha256 STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD[-TRAILER]), unsigned streaming PUT (STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER), SigV4 header (AWS4-HMAC-SHA256), SigV4 presigned (?X-Amz-Credential), JWT bearer, anonymous (no Authorization header at all) or unknown (an Authorization header in no known shape). Defines the signing constants signV4Algorithm, iso8601Format and yyyymmdd.
weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.when: Every authenticated route (inside iam.Auth / AuthSignatureOnly), AuthWithPublicRead's anonymous checks, the IAM POST matcher in the router, and setResponseHeaders (response-* overrides only for non-anonymous requests).
weed/s3api/s3api_auth.go.why: Consequence: authenticateRequestInternal dispatches on this result, so a misclassification sends a request to the wrong verifier or treats a signed request as anonymous. Design: the check order matters: streaming checks come before plain SigV4 because streaming uploads also carry an AWS4 Authorization header; 'unknown' is distinct from 'anonymous' so a garbled Authorization header is denied, never downgraded to anonymous access. Unsigned streaming only describes the body framing; the auth layer then looks again for the real credential (SigV4, JWT or none).

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.character: Per-gateway cache plus S3ApiServer accessors: BucketConfigCache (two size-capped LRUs, positive and negative) holding parsed BucketConfig values, the single entry→config mapping, and the read/patch API every bucket-aware path uses
gotchas: Building a config has side effects: newBucketConfigFromEntry calls syncBucketPolicyToEngine every time, including on the write path and the subscription refresher.

UpdateBucketMetadata (tags/CORS/encryption) is a read-modify-write that reads the CACHED config and then replaces the whole Entry.Content blob: last write wins across those three settings, and the base can be as stale as the subscription lag. updateBucketConfig instead re-reads the entry and patches only changed Extended keys.

Object Lock implies versioning everywhere (isVersioningEnabled, isVersioningConfigured, getVersioningState, the lifecycle-TTL 'versioned' check); applyBucketConfigToExtended never deletes object-lock keys once set.
KMSKeyCache/BucketKMSCache is effectively unused: only s3_sse_kms.go's uncalled bucket-key path would attach it (see s3_sse_kms.go issue note).
The lifecycle TTL fast path is parsed only when the bucket has ExtLifecycleTtlFastPathKey=true; a parse error yields nil (no TTL) rather than rejecting writes.
Both LRUs are capped at bucketCacheCapacity = 65536 buckets; evicted buckets reload from the filer on next access.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.if_broken: Every handler that branches on bucket state misbehaves: objects overwrite instead of versioning, WORM is not enforced, bucket policies are not evaluated, CORS headers are missing. A broken patch path either loses config writes or acknowledges writes that never landed.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.ux: Invisible when right. When wrong or stale: versioning or object-lock behavior that does not match what the client set, CORS preflights failing, a just-deleted bucket answering NoSuchBucket for up to the negative TTL after it is recreated on another gateway.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.what: Turns a bucket's filer entry into a BucketConfig (newBucketConfigFromEntry: versioning, ownership, ACL and its public-read flag, owner, creator identity, object-lock config, bucket policy, lifecycle XML and the optional lifecycle-TTL resolver, and tags/CORS/encryption decoded from the protobuf in Entry.Content), caches it (getBucketConfig) and writes it back. Two write paths: updateBucketConfig re-reads the entry and patches only changed Extended keys; setBucketMetadata replaces the whole Entry.Content blob (tags, CORS, encryption). Both go through patchBucketEntry, an ObjectTransaction PATCH_EXTENDED guarded by IF_EXISTS and routed to the bucket's owner filer. It also has the convenience readers (isVersioningEnabled/Configured, getVersioningState, isObjectLockEnabled, getBucketOwnership, getCORSConfiguration, checkVersionIdConfigured), proto↔CORS converters, and BucketKMSCache (per-bucket SSE-KMS data-key cache that zeroes plaintext on eviction).
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.when: getBucketConfig runs on nearly every bucket or object request, from auth (policy and ownership checks) to PUT/GET (versioning state). A cold load also synchronously backfills a pre-existing bucket policy into the advanced-IAM mirror (ensureBucketPolicyInIAM) before the IAM path evaluates it. updateBucketConfig runs on PutBucketVersioning, ownership, ACL, object-lock and lifecycle writes; setBucketMetadata on tagging, CORS and encryption writes.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config.go.why: Consequence: almost every request reads bucket config (versioning, ownership, policy, CORS), so without the cache each request would cost a filer lookup; with a wrong mapping a request silently runs under the wrong versioning or lock rules. Design: newBucketConfigFromEntry is the single mapping used by the read path, the write path and the metadata-subscription refresher, so a missed field cannot keep stale data. The author's example: a stale LifecycleTTL would keep stamping an irreversible volume TTL onto new writes. Writes are field-level patches routed to the owner filer so concurrent config writes serialize under one path lock instead of racing whole-entry rewrites, and IF_EXISTS keeps a PATCH on a deleted bucket from being acknowledged as a silent no-op. After a write the cache entry is invalidated, not refreshed, because the locally built config may be stale relative to a concurrent write. Consistency comes mainly from metadata-subscription events (auth_credentials_subscribe.go); the TTL is a safety net, and the negative cache's TTL is ttl/4 with a 30s floor. AWS compatibility: GetBucketVersioning returns exactly what is stored (empty means never configured, so no Status element), and Object Lock forces versioning Enabled whatever the stored flag says.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.character: Stub handlers for bucket configurations SeaweedFS does not store: analytics, inventory, intelligent-tiering and metrics
gotchas: There are no Put/Delete counterparts; writing these configurations still fails.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.if_broken: Bucket discovery in SDKs and IaC tools fails with MethodNotAllowed.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.ux: Tools that read every bucket setting keep working; nothing can actually be configured.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.what: After stubBucketGuard confirms the bucket exists (NoSuchBucket first, as AWS orders it), the Get* handlers answer NoSuchConfiguration and the List* handlers answer an empty, non-truncated list document in the S3 namespace.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.when: GET /<bucket>?analytics, ?inventory, ?intelligent-tiering and ?metrics, with or without an id.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_config_stubs.go.why: Consequence: AWS SDKs and tools such as Terraform's aws_s3_bucket probe these subresources during discovery; MethodNotAllowed would make them fail on a bucket that is otherwise fine. Design: an honest 'not configured' instead of a fake configuration. AWS compatibility: a never-configured bucket gets the same answers on AWS.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.character: The Get/Put/DeleteBucketCors handlers plus the adapters that plug the gateway into the cors middleware, including the global fallback built from -allowedOrigins
gotchas: PutBucketCors decodes the body straight from r.Body with no size cap; the 100-rule limit is checked only after the whole document is decoded.
Invalid rules answer InvalidRequest rather than AWS's MalformedXML / InvalidArgument codes.
CORS shares the metadata blob with tags and encryption, so it inherits that write path's read-modify-write race (see s3api_bucket_config.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.if_broken: CORS rules are not stored or not applied, so browser clients break, or a bucket's rules are silently replaced by the global fallback.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.ux: aws s3api put-bucket-cors works as on AWS; with -allowedOrigins set, buckets without their own rules still answer CORS.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.what: S3BucketChecker and S3CORSConfigGetter adapt the server to the cors package interfaces. getCORSMiddleware builds the middleware, and createFallbackCORSConfig turns the -allowedOrigins option into one permissive rule (all five methods, all headers, standard expose headers). GetBucketCors returns the stored configuration or NoSuchCORSConfiguration. PutBucketCors decodes and validates the XML and stores it through updateCORSConfiguration (the bucket-metadata path). DeleteBucketCors removes it and answers 204.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.when: GET/PUT/DELETE /<bucket>?cors; the fallback is built once when the router is set up.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_cors_handlers.go.why: Consequence: these settings decide which websites may call the bucket from a browser. Design: the configuration is stored in the bucket's metadata blob with tags and encryption (setBucketMetadata), so it is cached in BucketConfig and refreshed by the metadata subscription. The global fallback lets an operator enable browser access for every bucket without per-bucket configuration. AWS compatibility: same operations and status codes as S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handlers for bucket lifecycle and core bucket subresources, plus the AuthWithPublicRead middleware and bucket ownership/admin helpers
gotchas: AuthWithPublicRead's public-bucket fast paths call the handler WITHOUT iam.Auth, so scrubInternalHeaders does not run there; raw anonymous GET/HEAD object reads go through deferAnonymousObjectRead instead, which does scrub (via authenticateRequestInternal).
checkBucket only checks existence when auth is enabled; the ownership check (hasAccess) applies only when auth is DISABLED.
PutBucketAclHandler sleeps 50ms before answering.

DeleteBucketOwnershipControls rewrites the whole bucket entry with updateEntry instead of the patch path updateBucketConfig uses, and does not invalidate bucketConfigCache, so a concurrent config patch can be lost and this gateway can serve the old ownership until the metadata event arrives.
GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration falls back to synthesizing rules from legacy filer.conf collection TTLs when no lifecycle XML is stored; Put/Delete lifecycle clear those legacy day-TTLs first.
DeleteBucket prunes 'Action:bucket' grants from dynamic identities as best-effort bookkeeping on a 30s background context; static identities are never touched.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.if_broken: Buckets are created without the requested lock/versioning, deleted while still holding locked objects, listed to callers who should not see them, or public-read buckets stop serving anonymous reads.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.ux: Bucket create/delete/list semantics for every client and console; whether an anonymous browser can fetch from a public-read bucket; a lifecycle change that leaves objects stamped with a fast-path TTL gets a warning header.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.what: ListBuckets (served from the per-owner index when the identity's grants name every bucket it can reach, otherwise a paged scan of BucketsPath filtered per bucket; base64 continuation tokens; max 10000), PutBucket (name check, explicit-ACL parse, refuse table-bucket names, advisory collection listing with a 15s budget, mkdirExclusive with owner, ACL and object-lock-implies-versioning set atomically, owner-index add), DeleteBucket (refuse table buckets, block while object-locked objects remain or the bucket has user objects unless -allowDeleteBucketNotEmpty, recursive delete inside a retry budget, owner-index removal, prune IAM actions scoped to the bucket), HeadBucket, Get/PutBucketAcl, Get/Put/DeleteBucketLifecycleConfiguration, GetBucketLocation/RequestPayment, ownership controls, Get/PutBucketVersioning. Helpers: autoCreateBucket/handleAutoCreateBucket (PutObject into a missing bucket with -autoCreateBucket and Admin), existingBucketError (BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou vs BucketAlreadyExists), setBucketOwner, checkBucket/hasAccess, isUserAdmin/userCanAdminBucket, AuthWithPublicRead.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.when: PUT/DELETE/HEAD /bucket and the bucket-level ?acl, ?lifecycle, ?location, ?requestPayment, ?ownershipControls, ?versioning routes; GET / for ListBuckets. AuthWithPublicRead wraps GET/HEAD object, ListObjects and HeadBucket. autoCreateBucket runs from the PutObject and multipart paths.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go.why: Consequence: bucket creation and deletion set the ownership and lock invariants every later request relies on; a non-atomic create could leave a bucket without the object lock the client asked for. Design: object lock and versioning are written in the same CreateEntry as the bucket and rolled back if serialization fails; mkdirExclusive keeps a plain bucket from replacing a table bucket created in the check-to-create window; the collection listing is advisory only, because the filer resolves and drops the collection inside the delete. AWS compatibility: BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou is returned only for a repeat create by the same owner with no conflicting ACL or object-lock request; unrouted subresource PUT/DELETE answer NotImplemented instead of being treated as CreateBucket/DeleteBucket; a lifecycle with Transition rules answers NotImplemented; Suspended versioning is refused on object-lock buckets (InvalidBucketState); GetBucketVersioning omits Status when never configured.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.character: Small read-only bucket subresources that report 'not used' or a computed answer: policy status, request payment, accelerate, logging, notification, replication, website, plus the guard that stops unknown subresources from turning into a listing
gotchas: isPolicyPublic treats any condition as making a statement non-public, while AWS counts some conditions (such as aws:SourceArn) as still public.
The listing-parameter allowlist (listObjectsQueryParams) must grow with any new ListObjects parameter, or that request turns into NotImplemented.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.if_broken: Consoles and SDK helpers fail on bucket inspection, or unknown subresources return listings.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.ux: Tools that inspect bucket settings get sensible answers; 'requester pays' cannot be enabled.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.what: GetBucketPolicyStatus reports IsPublic when some Allow statement has Principal '*' and no conditions. PutBucketRequestPayment accepts only Payer=BucketOwner (body capped at 64 KiB). GetBucketAccelerateConfiguration answers Suspended. GetBucketLogging and GetBucketNotificationConfiguration answer empty documents. GetBucketReplication and GetBucketWebsite answer their not-found errors. unroutedBucketSubresource / unroutedSubresource name the first query key on a bucket GET that is neither a listing parameter nor a presign key, so ListObjects can answer NotImplemented instead of a listing.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.when: GET /<bucket>?policyStatus, ?accelerate, ?logging, ?notification, ?replication, ?website and PUT ?requestPayment; the unrouted check runs in the ListObjects catch-all.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_misc.go.why: Consequence: SDKs and consoles call these during bucket inspection, and an unknown subresource answered with a bucket listing silently tells the client something false (for example that a GET ?replication succeeded). Design: features SeaweedFS does not have report the same state AWS shows for a bucket that never enabled them. AWS compatibility: response element names and error codes match AWS.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_object_.character: The Put/GetObjectLockConfiguration handlers: a bucket's default retention and Object Lock enabled state
gotchas: Both Get paths set XMLNS on the configuration before marshaling; on the cached path that writes into the BucketConfig shared by concurrent requests.
ObjectLockEnabled must be 'Enabled' (any other value is malformed XML), so Object Lock cannot be switched off; a configuration without a Rule clears the default retention.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_object_.if_broken: New objects get the wrong default retention, or compliance checks report Object Lock missing on a locked bucket.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_object_.ux: aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration sets the default retention; buckets created without Object Lock refuse it.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_object_.what: PutObjectLockConfiguration requires the bucket to support Object Lock (isObjectLockAvailable; otherwise 409 InvalidBucketState), parses and validates the XML (ValidateObjectLockConfiguration, mapped to S3 errors), and stores it as BucketConfig.ObjectLockConfig through updateBucketConfig. GetObjectLockConfiguration returns the cached configuration. If the cache has none it re-reads the bucket entry, loads the configuration from its extended attributes and refreshes the whole cached BucketConfig from that entry; otherwise it answers ObjectLockConfigurationNotFoundError.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers_object_.why: Consequence: the default retention here is applied to every new object version in the bucket, so a wrong value either locks data that should be deletable or leaves compliance data unprotected. Design: the Get path re-reads the filer when the cache shows nothing, because a bucket created with Object Lock on another gateway may not have reached this cache yet, and reporting 'not found' there would mislead compliance tooling. AWS compatibility: 409 InvalidBucketState for buckets without Object Lock matches AWS and s3-tests.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.character: Storage helpers for a bucket's lifecycle configuration: the raw XML and the transition minimum-object-size setting
gotchas: The returned XML is a copy, so callers may modify it, but the stored version is what clients wrote, not a re-serialization.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.if_broken: Lifecycle rules are lost or not visible to the worker, so objects never expire, or expire under stale rules.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.ux: Lifecycle configuration round-trips byte for byte.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.what: Aliases the stored-key names and the size cap from the scheduler package. getStoredBucketLifecycleConfiguration returns a copy of the stored XML and the normalized X-Amz-Transition-Default-Minimum-Object-Size value (default all_storage_classes_128K). storeBucketLifecycleConfiguration and clearStoredBucketLifecycleConfiguration write them through updateBucketConfig.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.why: Consequence: GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration replays exactly these stored bytes, and the lifecycle worker reads the same keys, so the storage form is shared state. Design: the key names live in s3lifecycle/scheduler because callers outside the gateway read them too; this file only holds local shorthands. AWS compatibility: the transition minimum-object-size header is echoed back as AWS does.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.character: The warning logic for lifecycle changes on buckets using the TTL fast path, where objects already written keep the volume TTL they were stamped with
gotchas: The eligibility test duplicates NewLifecycleTTLResolver's filter (s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go); if the two drift, the warning fires for the wrong rules.
Clients ignore unknown headers, so the warning only helps operators who look at raw responses or logs.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.if_broken: Operators silently lose data they thought a lifecycle change had protected, or get false alarms on harmless edits.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.ux: The response carries a header naming the rules whose already-written objects will still expire on the old schedule.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.what: fastpathConfigChangeLeavesStampedObjects compares the old and new lifecycle XML (nil new means delete). It takes the rules that were fast-path eligible (Enabled, ExpirationDays > 0, no tag filter, fits int32 seconds) and matches them to new rules, first by ID, then by prefix and size filters. It returns a reason when an eligible rule was removed or disabled, had its filter changed, or was lengthened. The handlers put that reason in the X-Seaweed-Lifecycle-Fastpath-Warning response header.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.when: PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration and DeleteBucketLifecycle on buckets with the lifecycle TTL fast path enabled.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpa.why: Consequence: on the fast path an object's expiry is baked into its volume TTL at write time and cannot be taken back, so removing or extending a rule does not save objects already written; without a warning an operator would believe retention was extended. Design: shortening a rule and pure ID renames do not warn, because neither loses data. Tag-filtered rules are never on the fast path. AWS compatibility: none; this is a SeaweedFS-specific header.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.character: The bucket owner index under /buckets/.system/owners/<owner>/<bucket>, which lets ListBuckets serve one identity's buckets without scanning every bucket
gotchas: Ownership is keyed by identity name (AmzIdentityId); a user renamed through UpdateUser no longer finds the buckets indexed under the old name.
Admins, a bare List grant, wildcard action or resource grants and STS session requests never use the index; they still scan /buckets.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.if_broken: Users miss buckets they own in ListBuckets, or see deleted ones, depending on which write path broke.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.ux: ListBuckets stays fast for ordinary users regardless of the total number of buckets.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.what: The index holds zero-length files whose Crtime is the bucket's creation time, under an escaped owner directory (escapeOwnerName percent-encodes '/' and a leading dot). It is written in three ways: the bucket handlers write it synchronously, maintainBucketOwnerIndex applies /buckets metadata events, and startBucketOwnerIndexBackfill indexes pre-existing buckets, re-listing each page to drop buckets deleted meanwhile, then writes a .complete marker. bucketOwnerIndexReady caches that marker. listBucketsFromOwnerIndex merges the owned index entries with the buckets the identity's legacy actions name explicitly (after resolveGrantedBuckets checks visibility) and pages with a continuation token.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.when: CreateBucket and DeleteBucket handlers, every /buckets metadata event, the backfill once at startup, and ListBuckets for identities whose grants name only specific buckets (canListBucketsFromOwnerIndex).
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_owner_index.go.why: Consequence: ListBuckets for a non-admin identity used to scan all of /buckets; with tens of thousands of buckets that is slow and loads the filer on every call. Design: every write path is idempotent, so the synchronous writes, the subscription and racing backfills on several gateways cannot conflict, and readers keep scanning until the backfill marker exists, so a half-built index is never trusted.

weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.character: BucketPolicyEngine: the per-server wrapper (one instance on S3ApiServer, shared with IdentityAccessManagement) around policy_engine.PolicyEngine for bucket policies
gotchas: The engine is fed from the bucket config cache; a policy changed on another gateway only applies here after the metadata event rebuilds the config.
LoadBucketPolicy (from an entry) has no in-package callers besides tests; production loads go through LoadBucketPolicyFromCache.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.if_broken: Bucket policies stop applying (data exposed or legitimate access denied) or evaluation errors deny everything (callers fail closed on errors).
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.ux: Bucket policies written for AWS work unchanged: Allow, Deny, Condition and Principal blocks.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.what: Loads, replaces and deletes a bucket's policy document in the engine (from a bucket entry's Extended key or from the already-parsed cached document) and evaluates a request against it: resolves the fine-grained s3: action from the request (ResolveS3Action), builds the resource ARN, extracts condition values (source IP via trusted proxies, headers, tags, principal variables, JWT claims, original ACL grant headers, and the object's existing tags when an entry is passed), and for UploadPart / Complete / Abort looks up the SSE algorithm stored at CreateMultipartUpload so s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption conditions still apply. Returns (allowed, evaluated, err): evaluated=false means no matching statement.
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.when: Every authenticated request on a bucket with a policy (Phase 1 in authRequestWithAuthType), anonymous requests in AuthWithPublicRead, and handler rechecks with the object entry; policies are loaded when bucket configs are built (syncBucketPolicyToEngine).
weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_policy_engine.go.why: Consequence: bucket policies are the S3 resource-based access control; this is where they are actually enforced, in both auth phases (iam.Auth before the handler, checkPolicyWithEntry after the entry is loaded). Design: tri-state results let callers implement AWS semantics (explicit Deny wins, Allow can grant, no-match falls through to identity policies); the multipart SSE lookup exists because UploadPart requests carry no SSE header, so a 'Deny unless encrypted' policy would otherwise wrongly deny or allow parts. AWS compatibility: s3: action names, ARN resources and condition keys match AWS's.

weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.character: Per-route admission control: the global and per-bucket circuit breaker plus the concurrent-upload throttle, wrapped around every handler as cb.Limit
gotchas: Enabled and limitations are replaced on reload without taking the mutex while requests read them; under Go's memory model that is a data race, harmless only because the fields are word-sized.
Byte limits use r.ContentLength, so chunked uploads (ContentLength -1, counted as 0) bypass both the upload-bytes throttle and the bytes breaker.
The throttle re-reads the counters, unlocks, then increments, so several waiters woken together can overshoot the limit.
Interceptor is a seam that nothing in this repository sets.
weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.if_broken: Either no protection against overload, or counters that leak (never rolled back) and eventually reject every request for an action.
weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.ux: Throttled clients get 503 SlowDown when a breaker trips (the request-count and bytes breakers both use it), or simply slower uploads under the upload limits.
weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.what: NewCircuitBreaker loads /etc/s3/circuit_breaker.json from a filer (absent means disabled). Limit(handler, action) returns the wrapped handler. For ACTION_WRITE it first blocks on a condition variable while in-flight upload bytes exceed -concurrentUploadLimitMB or in-flight uploads reach -concurrentFileUploadLimit, then counts the request in. If the breaker is enabled, limit() checks four counters in order: bucket request count, bucket bytes, global request count, global bytes. It rejects with ErrTooManyRequest or ErrRequestBytesExceed (both 503 SlowDown) and rolls back the counters it took. An optional Interceptor wraps everything and runs even when the breaker is disabled.
weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.when: Every route registered with cb.Limit (almost all S3 routes; ownership-controls routes skip it). Reloaded when the config file changes (auth_credentials_subscribe.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_circuit_breaker.go.why: Consequence: without admission control a burst of large uploads exhausts memory and volume-server bandwidth for every tenant. Design: limits are configured per action and per bucket in the filer and reloaded live through the metadata subscription, so an operator can throttle one noisy bucket without a restart. Upload throttling waits rather than rejects, so clients are slowed instead of failed.

weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.character: The AWS IAM query API served on the S3 port: EmbeddedIamApi with 48 user, access-key, policy, group, tag and service-account actions (plus the 17 OIDC and role actions it hands to its two satellite files), the read-only gate, the persistence strategy and the IAM authorization rules (AuthorizeIamAction, AuthIamManagement)
gotchas: policyLock serializes actions within one gateway only. The full-save path (groups, service accounts, tags) is a whole-configuration read-modify-write, so two gateways changing groups at the same time can lose one change.

Service accounts authenticate as their parent identity (auth_credentials.go appends their key to the parent), so they always have the parent's current permissions. The Actions snapshot copied at CreateServiceAccount is stored but not used for authorization.

PutUserPolicy runs the document through getActions, so a Deny statement or a document with no s3: actions is rejected even though the runtime evaluates inline policies with Deny and Condition. PutGroupPolicy accepts the same document.
DeleteAccessKey answers 200 for a key or user that does not exist (AWS answers NoSuchEntity).
ListPolicies rejects any PathPrefix other than '/' with NotImplemented; policy paths are not tracked.
ExecuteAction's skipPersist is only ever false in production (DoActions is the only caller); the gRPC comment about callers is stale.

Authorization reads Action from r.Form while ExecuteAction reads r.PostForm. They agree because body values take precedence in r.Form; an Action only in the query string authorizes but executes as InvalidAction.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.if_broken: Credentials cannot be created, rotated or revoked through the API, or worse are created for the wrong identity. A missed reload makes a revoked key keep working until the next config refresh.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.issue_note: CreatePolicyVersion validates the new document with getActions (Allow-only, needs at least one s3: action); CreatePolicy validates only that it is JSON. A managed policy created with a Deny statement, or with only non-s3 actions, can therefore never be updated in place: the AWS Terraform provider updates aws_iam_policy through CreatePolicyVersion and gets MalformedPolicyDocument. Probe (NewEmbeddedIamApiForTest): CreatePolicy with an Allow + Deny document → 200; CreatePolicyVersion with the same document → 400 MalformedPolicyDocument 'not a valid effect: Deny'; an iam:GetUser-only document → 200 on create, 400 'no valid actions found' on version. The attached-policy evaluator enforces Deny, so getActions is a stale check here.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.ux: Users manage their own access keys without admin rights by default (self-service CreateAccessKey/DeleteAccessKey/ListAccessKeys/GetUser/UpdateAccessKey); everything else needs an iam:<Action> grant or admin. On a default install every write answers AccessDenied 'IAM write operations are disabled on this server' until -iam.readOnly=false.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.what: DoActions parses the form, injects the caller as the implicit UserName for self-service actions and CreatedBy for CreateServiceAccount, then calls ExecuteAction. ExecuteAction serializes every action under policyLock, refuses writes on a read-only gateway, dispatches OIDC and role actions first, then loads the whole S3ApiConfiguration from the credential manager and runs the handler on it in memory. Persistence is mixed. Users, access keys, inline user policies and status are written as targeted single-identity writes (CreateUser, persistIdentity, persistRenamedIdentity, deleteIdentity). Managed and group inline policies go straight to the credential manager. Groups, service accounts and user tags fall through to a full SaveConfiguration (changed=true). Every write is followed by a reload of the in-memory identity maps. The policy handlers keep a single 'v1' version per managed policy (CreatePolicyVersion replaces it and requires SetAsDefault=true). getActions flattens an Allow-only policy into legacy 'Action:bucket/path' strings; PutUserPolicy stores the real document and recomputes the identity's flattened Actions from all inline policies. The file also defines AuthorizeIamAction (self-service rules, iam:<Action> grants, the target-user ARN), AuthIamManagement (authentication for the standalone weed iam server) and writeIamErrorResponse (IAM error code → HTTP status).
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.when: Every authenticated POST / whose Action is not an STS action reaches DoActions via UnifiedPostHandler (s3api_server.go), which authorizes with AuthorizeIamAction first. AuthIamManagement wraps the same flow for the standalone weed iam server. Enabled by default (-iam=true) but read-only by default (-iam.readOnly=true).
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam.go.why: Consequence: this is the control plane for every credential the gateway accepts. A wrong check here mints keys for the wrong user, and a lost write drops a user's keys or policies. Design: one gateway can be both the S3 endpoint and its IAM endpoint, so aws-cli / Terraform IAM calls work against SeaweedFS directly. Targeted writes replaced whole-configuration rewrites so a change touches one identity's record and propagates alone (Postgres needs RenameUser to rename inside one transaction because of FK constraints). The authorized target is read from the same body field the handler acts on (iamTargetUserName / r.PostForm), so a query-string UserName cannot steer authorization. IAM management is checked as iam:<Action>, never as an S3 data-plane action. AWS compatibility: action names, member.N encoding, AKIA/ABIA key formats, DeleteConflict on users with keys or groups with members, idempotent Attach*, and the 'cannot delete the default version' answer follow AWS. SetUserStatus and the service-account actions are SeaweedFS extensions.

weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.character: Satellite of the embedded IAM API: the nine OpenIDConnectProvider actions, dispatched before the S3ApiConfiguration load because providers live in the advanced-IAM manager's OIDC store, not in the identity config
gotchas: extractMemberList and extractTags stop at the first missing index, so a list with a gap (member.1, member.3) is silently truncated after member.1.

GetOpenIDConnectProvider maps every store error to NoSuchEntity (404), including transient store failures; UpdateOpenIDConnectProviderThumbprint maps unknown errors to InvalidInput, the other mutations to ServiceFailure.
Tags come back in map order, so Create/Get responses list them in a different order each time.
The ARN uses the STS service's configured AccountId; if that is empty the ARN has no account segment.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.if_broken: Web-identity federation cannot be managed at runtime: new IdPs or client IDs cannot be added, and a revoked client ID keeps being trusted until someone edits the store directly.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.ux: An operator registers an IdP (Keycloak, GitHub Actions, Dex) with the same commands they use against AWS. Without advanced IAM configured, every call fails with ServiceFailure 'OIDC provider store not configured'.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.what: isOIDCProviderAction recognizes Get/List/Create/Delete OpenIDConnectProvider, Add/RemoveClientID, UpdateThumbprint and Tag/Untag. dispatchOIDCProviderAction resolves the integration.IAMManager (oidcIAMManager: only when the server runs advanced IAM and its integration exposes GetIAMManager) and calls one handler per action. Create requires Url and at least one ClientIDList.member.N, derives the provider ARN from the STS account ID and the URL (integration.DeriveOIDCProviderARN) and stores an OIDCProviderRecord. The other mutations take OpenIDConnectProviderArn (requireProviderArn) and call the matching IAMManager method. The file also has the AWS query-list parsers extractMemberList (<prefix>.member.N) and extractTags (Tags.member.N.Key/Value), and oidcMutationError, which maps a static (config-file) provider to UnmodifiableEntity and a missing one to NoSuchEntity.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.when: Only on a POST / IAM request (UnifiedPostHandler → DoActions → ExecuteAction) whose Action is one of the nine names, after AuthorizeIamAction has checked iam:<Action>. On a read-only gateway (-iam.readOnly, the default) only Get and List get through.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_oidc.go.why: Consequence: these providers decide which external IdPs AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity trusts, so a provider created here immediately widens who can obtain STS credentials. Design: a provider defined in the IAM config file is reloaded from it at every start, so the API refuses to change it (UnmodifiableEntity) instead of accepting an edit that would silently revert. AWS compatibility: action names, parameter encoding (member.N lists) and error codes follow the AWS IAM query API, so aws-cli, the SDKs and Terraform's aws_iam_openid_connect_provider work unchanged.

weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.character: Satellite of the embedded IAM API: the eight IAM role actions, run against the advanced-IAM manager's role store with atomic read-modify-write updates
gotchas: CreateRole has to check for a same-named config-file role with GetRole first, because static roles are served beside the store and its create-if-absent cannot see them.

Attaching checks that the managed policy exists, but the policy can be deleted afterwards. DeletePolicy guards against this with integration.RolesAttachingPolicy, which cannot see roles that exist only in a peer gateway's config file.
A role stored before role IDs were recorded is reported with integration.StaticRoleID instead of a stored ID.
oidcIAMManager is shared with the OIDC file: without advanced IAM every role action is ServiceFailure 'role store not configured'.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.if_broken: Roles cannot be created or changed at runtime. A broken atomic update would let two gateways overwrite each other's trust-policy or attachment changes, or resurrect a deleted role.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.ux: Lets operators manage roles for AssumeRole and web-identity federation from aws-cli or Terraform. Unsupported features (paths, tags) fail loudly with InvalidInput instead of being dropped.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.what: dispatchRoleAction handles CreateRole, GetRole, ListRoles, DeleteRole, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy, Attach/DetachRolePolicy and ListAttachedRolePolicies through the same IAMManager the OIDC actions use. Every write goes through IAMManager.UpdateRole, a compare-and-retry update on the role store where a nil result deletes the role. CreateRole validates the name, rejects Path other than '/' and any Tags.*, parses and validates the trust policy (parseTrustPolicy → policy.ValidateTrustPolicyDocument), applies PrepareRoleDefinition (MaxSessionDuration must be 3600–43200 when set) and creates only if absent. DeleteRole refuses with DeleteConflict while managed policies are attached. AttachRolePolicy checks that the managed policy exists in the credential manager and caps attachments at MaxManagedPoliciesPerRole. toIAMRole renders the role, with the trust policy URL-encoded as AWS returns it.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.when: On a POST / IAM request whose Action is a role action, after authorization; dispatched in ExecuteAction right after the OIDC provider actions and before the S3ApiConfiguration load. Read-only gateways serve only GetRole, ListRoles and ListAttachedRolePolicies.
weed/s3api/s3api_embedded_iam_role.go.why: Consequence: a role's trust policy decides who may AssumeRole into it and its attached policies decide what the resulting session can do, so a lost update here silently changes privileges. Design: changes run inside the store's atomic update, so a change made on one gateway is neither lost to a concurrent change on another nor written over a concurrent delete; the 'has attached policies' check is evaluated against the role as it is at delete time. Roles from the IAM config file are refused (UnmodifiableEntity) because the next start would revert any API change. AWS compatibility: response shapes, the URL-encoded AssumeRolePolicyDocument and the DeleteConflict / LimitExceeded / EntityAlreadyExists codes match AWS, which Terraform's aws_iam_role relies on.

weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing filer_pb.FilerClient (the gateway's filer connection with failover), plus stateless response-writer helpers
gotchas: If s3a.filerClient is nil (initialization/tests only) withFilerClient falls back to a direct single-filer connection with no failover and context.Background().
The exported WithFilerClient carries no context (filer_pb.FilerClient's signature), so it runs with a Background budget; use withFilerClient(ctx, …) when a deadline exists.
A preferred owner outside the static filer list is not health-tracked by filerClient; markOwnerUnreachable (routed_read.go) is what makes route-by-key reads skip it for 2s.
writeSuccessResponseEmpty does not call s3err.PostLog, unlike the XML writers.
weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.if_broken: Replaying non-idempotent calls could double-apply writes; failing over on NotFound could serve stale or resurrected objects; counting caller timeouts as filer failures would cascade into every filer marked unhealthy and object reads failing gateway-wide.
weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.ux: With several filers, a dead filer costs the client a slightly slower request instead of a 5xx; reads routed to a key's owner see the client's own just-written object.
weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.what: Two things. (1) The gateway's path to the filer over gRPC: withFilerClient -> withFilerClientFailover tries candidate filers in order (preferred route owner, then the current filer, then healthy, then unhealthy ones), records each success or failure in the filerClient health tracker, and switches the current filer after a successful failover. receiveTrackingConn wraps the gRPC conn to note whether any reply already reached fn. (2) Thin writers over s3err (writeSuccessResponseXML/XMLBytes/Empty, writeFailureResponse) and validateContentMd5.
weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.when: Every filer RPC: lookups, listings, creates, deletes, ObjectTransaction. `preferred` is set by the route-by-key paths (s3api_object_routed_read/write.go); the response writers end almost every handler.
weed/s3api/s3api_handlers.go.why: Design: failover happens only on transport errors, and only before any reply has reached fn. A reached filer's ErrNotFound is authoritative, because fanning out could resurrect a peer's not-yet-replicated tombstone. Once part of a reply was consumed, replaying would duplicate what fn accumulated (half a listing, say), so the error is surfaced instead. replayable=false (committed transactions) runs fn only on a channel that just proved Ready within 2s and stops on any error once fn ran, because a lost reply cannot be told apart from an applied commit. A caller's own context expiring is not recorded against the filer: otherwise a slow upstream would flag every filer and open the circuit for unrelated reads. Consequence: every filer RPC the gateway makes goes through here.

weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing credential vending for the Iceberg REST catalog (an STS AssumeRole on the caller's behalf, scoped to one table prefix)
gotchas: Returns (nil, nil), not an error, when no role is configured: callers must treat that as 'vending disabled'.
stsSigningKey defined here is also the fingerprint key for StoredCredentialFingerprint; rotating the STS signing key invalidates all bound vended sessions.
weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.if_broken: Engines either cannot obtain credentials (vending fails) or obtain credentials broader than the table (data exposure across tables).
weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.ux: Query engines get short-lived, table-scoped S3 credentials from the catalog instead of needing the user's own keys.
weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.what: VendTableCredentials (off until SetIcebergCredentialRole configures a role) assumes that role for the authenticated principal through STS AssumeRoleForPrincipal with an inline session policy limited to s3://bucket/prefix/* (read-only → GetObject only; read-write adds Put/Delete/AbortMultipartUpload/ListMultipartUploadParts), ListBucket only under that prefix, and GetBucketLocation. It refuses wildcard or whole-bucket scopes, names the session iceberg-<principal>-<prefix> plus a hash tag of the caller's access key (≤64 chars), records the provider 'iceberg-catalog', and binds the session to the stored access key and an HMAC fingerprint of its secret when the caller used a stored key.
weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.when: Called by the Iceberg REST catalog (weed/s3api/iceberg) when a client requests table credentials (X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation: vended-credentials); STS sessions it mints are later validated on every SigV4 request carrying their token.
weed/s3api/s3api_iceberg_credentials.go.why: Consequence: Iceberg engines (Spark, Trino, Snowflake) ask the catalog for credentials to read/write table files; vending the caller's own long-term key would hand out far broader access than one table. Design: the session policy narrows the role to one table location; binding to the stored key means revoking or rotating that key also kills vended sessions (validateSTSSessionToken → vendedSessionKeyLive), so vended credentials cannot outlive the credential that requested them. The fingerprint is keyed with the STS signing key so the token holder gains no offline oracle on the secret.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.character: S3ApiServer helpers that move anonymous object-read authorization from the middleware to the handler, once the exact entry being served is known; a context-key marker type
gotchas: The context flag cannot be set by clients; only deferAnonymousObjectRead sets it.
A version file's physical filer path (key.versions/v_<id>) is refused as a key, so GetObjectVersion policies on the logical key cannot be bypassed.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.if_broken: Either public objects become unreadable anonymously, or private objects (or their existence) leak to anonymous callers.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.ux: Anonymous downloads of public objects and website-style hosting; anonymous callers get 403 (not 404) for missing keys in buckets they cannot list.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.what: deferAnonymousObjectRead marks raw anonymous GET/HEAD object reads (auth enabled, action Read, not a subresource, resolving to s3:GetObject or s3:GetObjectVersion, not SOSAPI) with a context flag. It drops unsigned X-Amz-Security-Token values and runs authenticateRequestInternal, which scrubs internal headers and resolves the configured anonymous identity if any. authorizeAnonymousObjectRead then decides against the served entry: deny physical .versions paths and delete markers; bucket policy with the entry's tags; explicit identity-side denies; the anonymous identity's own grants; the object ACL (unless BucketOwnerEnforced); finally the bucket's public-read flag. authorizeAnonymousBucketList and writeAnonymousAwareNotFound make a missing key indistinguishable from a denied one unless the bucket is anonymously listable.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.when: Inside AuthWithPublicRead before falling back to iam.Auth; the deferred handler (GET/HEAD object, directory objects, streaming of freshly cached remote entries) calls recheckPolicyWithObjectEntry, which routes marked requests to authorizeAnonymousObjectRead.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_anonymous_read.g.why: Consequence: without the deferral, a public object in a private bucket (object ACL or a tag-conditioned policy) could never be read anonymously, and a missing key would reveal itself with 404 vs 403. Design: authorization runs against the same entry used for the response (including conditional and versioned reads), so a race between check and serve cannot hand out an object the check never saw. Explicit policy denies beat every public grant. Each check runs on a synthesized request of fixed shape, so a caller's query parameters (?policy, ?prefix) cannot retarget the action. AWS compatibility: object ACLs are honored for legacy buckets without ownership controls; BucketOwnerEnforced disables them.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handlers for GetObject and HeadObject plus the read-side streaming engine (range parsing, direct volume-server streaming, inline SSE decryption, remote-mount stream-through), with stateless helpers shared by the listing and copy code
gotchas: decryptSSECChunkView returns the chunk's raw (still encrypted) bytes when an SSE-C chunk has no per-chunk metadata; the comment says the range path 'should not hit this', but nothing guards it.
Dead helpers in this file: NewMultipartSSEReader/MultipartSSEReader and cacheRemoteObjectForStreaming (the 20s-timeout variant) have no non-test callers.

SSE-KMS stores the BASE IV per chunk (decrypt applies ChunkOffset), SSE-S3 stores the already-ADJUSTED IV, SSE-C stores a random per-part IV plus PartOffset; pre-adjusting a KMS IV applies the offset twice and corrupts ranges across part boundaries.
The implicit-directory 404 on HEAD applies only to non-versioned buckets and keys without a trailing slash.
Remote-mount fallback is used only for the null/current version (shouldFallBackToRemote) and only when the remote size equals the entry size.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.if_broken: Clients receive corrupted or ciphertext bytes, truncated bodies with a 200, deleted objects resurrected (delete markers ignored), or objects visible to callers that a tag-conditioned policy denies.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.issue_note: GetObjectHandler and HeadObjectHandler each carry a near-verbatim ~90-line copy of versioned entry resolution (specific version → null delete marker → quick .versions/ probe → getLatestObjectVersion fallback → version id extraction → delete-marker response). A fix to how either handler resolves the current version does not reach the other.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.ux: Download behavior: status 200/206/304/404/412, Range and partNumber semantics, ETag, Last-Modified, Content-Type, user metadata, x-amz-version-id, lock headers, SSE headers, Retry-After on uncached remote objects.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.what: GetObjectHandler/HeadObjectHandler: table-bucket guard → SOSAPI virtual objects → versionId sanity → directory-marker objects → conditional headers → entry resolution (versioned: a specific version, the null delete marker, or latest via a quick .versions/ probe then getLatestObjectVersion; non-versioned: route-by-key lookup) → delete-marker answer → phase-2 policy recheck with the entry's tags → version and lock headers → stream. streamFromVolumeServers reads chunks straight from volume servers through the shared ReaderCache and defers the status line until the first byte is read (commitOnFirstWrite), so a missing needle becomes a clean 5xx instead of a broken 200. streamFromVolumeServersWithSSE validates SSE-C keys or loads SSE-KMS/S3 metadata, then decrypts either the whole object (single-part or a lazy multipart reader that applies per-chunk IVs) or only the chunks a Range touches. Objects of remote-mounted storage are cached in the background, streamed from the origin while uncached, or answered 503 + Retry-After: 2. Also: setResponseHeaders (metadata→headers filtering, tag count, checksum on x-amz-checksum-mode, response-* overrides only for signed requests), partNumber→byte-range mapping, detectPrimarySSEType, toFilerPath, newListEntry, resolveObjectEntry.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.when: GET/HEAD /bucket/key (wrapped in AuthWithPublicRead so anonymous public-read can pass). The streaming and decrypt helpers are also used by copy (getEncryptedStreamFromVolumes, cacheRemoteObjectForCopy) and listing (newListEntry).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers.go.why: Consequence: every object read goes through here, so a mistake is wrong bytes, leaked metadata, or decrypted data served to the wrong caller. Design: reading volume servers directly skips the filer proxy (author notes ~19ms saved per request). Deferring headers until the first byte lets fetch or decrypt failures become proper S3 errors. Version and lock headers are written only after the phase-2 policy check, so a denied caller learns nothing. AWS compatibility: a bare directory path or a 0-byte object with children answers 404 so s3fs/PyArrow and Hadoop clients fall back to LIST discovery; directories without data answer application/x-directory for Flink's presto S3 FS; tag, ACL and lock metadata never leak as headers; stored checksums are returned only for full-object reads, because partial responses would fail SDK validation; anonymous requests cannot use response-* overrides.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handlers for the multipart upload API (Create, UploadPart, Complete, Abort, ListParts, ListMultipartUploads); the storage logic lives in filer_multipart.go
gotchas: AbortMultipartUploadHandler calls s3err.WriteEmptyResponse (which already posts the audit log) and then s3err.PostLog again, so every abort emits two audit records.
Encryption parameters reach putToFiler as internal request headers (SeaweedFSSSEKMSBaseIVHeader, SeaweedFSSSES3KeyDataHeader…); this relies on iam.Auth scrubbing client-supplied copies.
Upload ids are deterministic per key (sha1 of the key) plus a random suffix; legacy ids without the suffix are still accepted.
getBucketMultipartResources / getObjectResources keep parsing after an invalid number and report the error code alongside a zero value.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.if_broken: Large uploads fail or complete into corrupted or undecryptable objects; aborted uploads leave orphan parts consuming storage.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.issue_note: NewMultipartUploadHandler passes isVersioningEnabled(bucket) as the objectLockEnabled argument of validateObjectLockHeaders (PutObject, CopyObject, POST policy and extract pass isObjectLockEnabled). On a versioning-enabled bucket WITHOUT Object Lock, x-amz-object-lock-mode/retain-until/legal-hold are therefore accepted (for callers holding the retention/legal-hold permission) instead of rejected; createMultipartUpload stores them on the upload entry and completion copies all upload-entry Extended keys onto the final object (filer_multipart.go). The object then reports retention in GET/HEAD headers and GetObjectRetention, but enforceObjectLockProtections skips buckets without Object Lock, so the 'locked' object can be deleted.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.ux: aws s3 cp/sync and SDK multipart uploads of large files; ETags of parts; checksum algorithm echo on Create.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.what: NewMultipartUploadHandler validates key length, SSE headers, bucket (auto-creating if allowed), table-bucket layout, object-lock headers, Cache-Control/Expires and the upload ACL, then creates the upload. PutObjectPartHandler validates the upload id against the key (sha1(key) plus an optional _<32 hex> suffix), replays the upload's SSE-KMS or SSE-S3 parameters (key id, encryption context, base IV, key data) from the upload directory entry into internal request headers, enforces the upload's checksum algorithm, writes the part to <bucket>/.uploads/<uploadId>/<NNNN>_<uuid>.part through putToFiler (with the object's path as storage destination), then re-checks that the upload was not aborted meanwhile (cleaning up its own part if it was). Complete/Abort/List handlers parse parameters and delegate. Also: genUploadsFolder, genPartUploadPath, checkUploadId, getMultipartSSEAlgorithm (used by the bucket policy engine for s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption conditions on UploadPart).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.when: POST ?uploads, PUT ?partNumber&uploadId (without a copy source), POST ?uploadId, DELETE ?uploadId, GET ?uploadId, GET ?uploads.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.why: Consequence: multipart is how every large object (>5 GB, or above SDK thresholds) is written, so failures here break large uploads for all SDKs. Design: encryption is decided once at Create and replayed per part from the upload entry, so all parts share one key and base IV and the completed object decrypts as one stream (parts use offsets from the base IV, never re-evaluating bucket defaults). Part files get a UUID suffix so a retried UploadPart of the same number never overwrites a part still referenced by an in-flight complete. checkUploadStillOpen closes the race where an Abort lands while a part is being written, which would otherwise leave an orphan part. AWS compatibility: part numbers 1..10000, max-uploads/max-parts defaults of 10000, ListMultipartUploads with a key-marker outside the prefix answers NotImplemented.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handler (PutObjectHandler) plus putToFiler, the shared object-write engine reused by multipart parts, copy and versioned writes; also hosts conditional-header evaluation, object-lock header validation and bucket-default encryption/retention
gotchas: Internal metadata reaches putToFiler as request headers (ExtVersionIdKey, object-lock keys); this is only safe because iam.Auth scrubs client-supplied copies first (scrubInternalHeaders).
Bucket default encryption is skipped for multipart part writes (withMultipartPart context flag): encryption is decided at CreateMultipartUpload and replayed via headers.
lifecycleTTLSec is non-zero only for top-level non-versioned PutObject; parts and copy-parts must pass 0 or their TTL clock would start before completion.
Parts (object == "") are never manifestized because completion rebases chunk offsets, which manifest chunks cannot express.
updateLatestVersionInDirectory retries the .versions lookup 8 times with 100ms·2^n backoff (up to ~12.7s total) and refuses to move the latest pointer backwards to an older version id.
A routed PUT that a filer answers PRECONDITION_FAILED with a conditionAltKey is resent once against the entry the read path serves, for filers that ignore condition_alt_key.
partOffset is hardcoded to 0 for every SSE call, including multipart parts; for SSE-S3 this makes all parts of an upload share one keystream (see the s3api_put_handlers.go issue note).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.if_broken: Uploads fail or, worse, report success for objects that are not stored or that point at deleted chunks; versioned buckets lose versions; WORM retention is bypassed by overwrites; encrypted objects become unreadable.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.issue_note: putToFiler validates x-amz-storage-class only after UploadReaderInChunks has stored the whole body, and returns ErrInvalidStorageClass without calling deleteOrphanedChunks, so every PutObject/UploadPart with an invalid storage class leaks its chunks on the volume servers. Tags are validated before the upload ('so a failed request leaves nothing behind'), and CopyObject validates storage class up front (s3api_object_handlers_copy.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.ux: What an S3 client sees on upload: ETag, x-amz-version-id, SSE and checksum echo headers, BadDigest / InvalidDigest / PreconditionFailed / IncompleteBody / ClientDisconnected / InvalidStorageClass errors, and 503 instead of a false success when a commit's outcome cannot be proven.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.what: PutObjectHandler validates the request (copy-source/partNumber misuse, Content-MD5, key length, table-bucket layout, conditional headers, bucket policy, SSE headers, Cache-Control/Expires), then branches: a trailing-slash key ≤1KB becomes an explicit directory marker (mkdir under the object write lock); otherwise it writes by versioning state (Enabled → putVersionedObject into <key>.versions/, Suspended → putSuspendedVersioningObject as the 'null' version, never-configured → plain putToFiler with an optional lifecycle TTL). putToFiler streams the body through MD5 and optional CRC/SHA hashers, applies SSE-C/KMS/S3 or bucket-default encryption, uploads chunks straight to volume servers (chunk size follows the filer's -maxMB, default 8 MiB), writes per-chunk SSE metadata, builds the entry (ETag, write id, checksum, owner, ACL, version id, lock fields, user metadata, tags, storage class), manifestizes chunks, and commits: routed to the key's owner filer as an ObjectTransaction when possible, else CreateEntry under the distributed object write lock. Uncertain outcomes go through createAfterAmbiguousRoute / confirmCreateLanded before any chunk cleanup.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.when: PUT /bucket/key with no copy source or multipart query. putToFiler is also called by UploadPart (s3api_object_handlers_multipart.go), copy paths and the versioned and suspended helpers here. checkConditionalHeaders(ForReads) run in GET/HEAD/PUT/copy handlers.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.why: Consequence: PutObject is the main write path, and putToFiler is also the write core of UploadPart, CopyObject and versioned writes, so a regression here is data loss or corruption across all writes. Design: chunks upload on context.Background() so a client disconnect cannot leave a half-written object. A failed create does not prove the entry is absent (a lost reply can hide a commit, #11366; the filer can fail after inserting, #11387), so the entry's presence, not the error class, decides whether the uploaded chunks are orphaned. Recovery refuses to re-commit when a concurrent write superseded the entry or the chunks cannot be verified, because that would store an entry pointing at reclaimed needles. Each entry carries a fresh SeaweedFSWriteId because an empty object has no chunks to identify it. Conditional creates are never replayed once possibly sent: a lost commit followed by a delete would let IF_NOT_EXISTS recreate an entry whose chunks were already freed. AWS compatibility: a PutObject ETag is always the plain MD5 even when auto-chunked; object-lock headers require s3:PutObjectRetention / s3:PutObjectLegalHold, not just s3:PutObject; conditional headers follow RFC 7232 precedence; GET/HEAD on a missing key stays 404 under conditions; suspended versioning returns no x-amz-version-id.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing object retention, legal hold and WORM enforcement, plus the XML types for Retention, LegalHold and ObjectLockConfiguration
gotchas: setObjectRetention and setObjectLegalHold are an unconditional read-check-write (getEntry → checks → updateEntry of the whole entry), not under the object write lock or an IF_ENTRY_EQUAL condition, so two concurrent retention updates race and a concurrent metadata change on the same entry can be overwritten.
getObjectEntry uses isVersioningEnabled (Enabled or object lock), so for Suspended buckets without a versionId it reads the plain object path.
A corrupt retention timestamp makes getObjectRetention fail, but enforceObjectLockOnEntry only logs it and treats the object as not under retention.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.if_broken: Locked objects can be deleted or overwritten (compliance violation), or unlocked objects become undeletable.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.ux: Clients see AccessDenied when deleting or overwriting locked data, and Get/PutObjectRetention / LegalHold behave like AWS's.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.what: get/setObjectRetention and get/setObjectLegalHold read and write ExtObjectLockModeKey / ExtRetentionUntilDateKey (unix seconds) / ExtLegalHoldKey on the right entry: the named version, the latest version file under .versions/ when versioning is enabled, or the plain object. setObjectRetention refuses to change the mode or shorten the date of a COMPLIANCE lock, and of a GOVERNANCE lock without bypass; it also stamps entry.WormEnforcedAtTsNs. enforceObjectLockOnEntry/Protections is the WORM gate used by deletes and overwrites: an active legal hold or COMPLIANCE retention always blocks, GOVERNANCE blocks unless x-amz-bypass-governance-retention: true AND the caller holds s3:BypassGovernanceRetention for that key. Also: isObjectEntryMiss (a not-found that is not a transient Unavailable), the DefaultRetention XML unmarshaller that tracks whether Days/Years were present, and the Max retention limits (36500 days / 100 years).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.when: PUT/GET ?retention and ?legal-hold (the handlers in s3api_object_handlers_retention.go / _legal_hold.go); enforceObjectLockProtections from DeleteObject(s), non-versioned PutObject/overwrite paths, the directory-marker path, and lifecycle deletes (s3api_internal_lifecycle.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.why: Consequence: this is the WORM guarantee; if it fails open, data under COMPLIANCE retention (which even admins must not delete) can be deleted or overwritten. Design: the bypass header alone is not enough: the permission is re-checked per key through authorizeObjectKeyAction, so a GOVERNANCE lock cannot be bypassed by anyone with plain write access. AWS compatibility: COMPLIANCE can only be extended, GOVERNANCE can be changed with bypass, legal hold is independent of retention; DaysSet/YearsSet distinguish 'absent' from '0' so Days=0 is rejected as InvalidRetentionPeriod, like AWS.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.character: S3ApiServer methods for read-your-writes lookups; holds a per-server TTL map of unreachable owners (s3a.unreachableOwners, sync.Map)
gotchas: routableWriteOwner (routed_write.go) is the single source of the owner; both sides must hash the same route key or reads miss writes.
The prior-owner probe happens only on ErrNotFound and only once; transport errors go through the normal failover walk instead.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.if_broken: Reads go to arbitrary filers and intermittently miss fresh writes or serve the old version; with the prior-owner probe broken, keys moved by a ring change briefly 404.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.ux: Read-after-write consistency in multi-filer deployments: a client that just PUT an object can GET it immediately.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.what: Reads an object's entry, or entries scoped to it (its .versions directory and version files), preferring the filer that owns the key's writes on the hash ring: getObjectEntryRoutedByKey, getObjectScopedEntryRoutedByKey, listObjectScopedEntriesRoutedByKey. If the owner says not-found during a rebalance it probes the key's prior owner once. Also keeps the 2s 'owner recently unreachable' marks and lookupEntryPreferringOwner / lookupEntryOnFiler for single-filer reads.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.when: GET/HEAD object and the versioning paths resolve entries through here when an objectWriteLockClient (ring) is configured; without one it reduces to plain getEntry/list.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.why: Consequence: with multiple filers, writes commit on the key's owner and replicate asynchronously; reading from any other filer right after a PUT could return 404 or the previous version. Design: unreachableOwnerTTL = 2s is long enough to spare a dead owner a dial on every request and short enough to resume owner-first reads soon after it or the ring recovers. lookupEntryPreferringOwner never swaps the owner for a healthier peer, since that would read behind the write the caller just made.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.character: S3ApiServer methods that turn object writes into ObjectTransaction RPCs on the key's owner filer, plus stateless builders for write conditions
gotchas: routeWriteCondition refuses to route a conditional write to a unique version path: a conditional versioned write must check the latest version, which only the lock path does.
routedObjectOwner deliberately returns no owner for versioned or object-lock buckets so WORM checks stay on the lock path.
routedUploadRemoval keeps a gateway-side exists() check because older filers ignore the mutation's upload-exists condition during rolling upgrades.
routedSelfCopy treats FailedPrecondition/NotFound as authoritative owner answers (no replay, owner not marked down).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.if_broken: Writes to the same key race (lost updates, both If-None-Match:* PUTs succeeding); a mismatched route key makes the filer forward to the wrong owner; a replayed transaction could re-apply mutations over a write that landed in between.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.ux: Concurrent writers to one key get consistent last-writer or precondition-failed answers instead of torn state; conditional PUTs behave like AWS's.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.what: Computes an object's ring route key (objectRouteKey), its owner filer (routableWriteOwner; routedObjectOwner for the unversioned-delete fast path) and sends atomic ObjectTransactions to it: routedPut (PUT plus optional finalize mutations such as RECOMPUTE_LATEST), routedMkFile/writeMultipartObject (multipart completion), routedDelete, routedSelfCopy (metadata-only copy guarded by IF_ENTRY_EQUAL). It turns HTTP conditional headers into filer WriteConditions evaluated under the owner's per-path lock (buildWriteCondition with RFC 7232 precedence; buildDeleteCondition honors If-Match only).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.when: PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload, DeleteObject (unversioned fast path), CopyObject onto itself, and versioned finalize paths call these when routableWriteOwner returns an owner; with no objectWriteLockClient the callers fall back to the distributed-lock path and plain mkFile.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.why: Design: all writes to one object (versioned, suspended or not) share one route key and owner, so they serialize under one path lock and conditional writes (If-Match, If-None-Match: *) are checked atomically at the filer instead of racing in the gateway. A trailing-slash marker key ('dir/') hashes to the same owner as 'dir'. Transactions are not replayable: failover only crosses a channel that never came up, and each logical transaction carries one RequestId so a retry replays the recorded outcome instead of re-applying mutations. Multipart completion removes the upload directory inside the same transaction, with an upload-exists precondition, so an abort/lifecycle/s3.clean.uploads that removed the directory first fails the commit instead of publishing an object over freed chunks. Consequence: with a ring configured, this is how every routed object write lands.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.character: S3ApiServer helpers that resolve the ACL an object upload will carry (stashed in the request context) plus a stateless request rewriter for policy evaluation
gotchas: When auth is disabled but a bucket policy exists, an explicit ACL is still checked against the policy for both Write and WriteAcp.
putObjectACLPolicyRequest only rewrites requests that resolve to s3:PutObject; other actions pass through unchanged.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.if_broken: Objects are stored with the wrong owner or grants (public by mistake, or unreadable by the bucket owner), or ACL-conditioned bucket policies can be bypassed.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.ux: x-amz-acl / x-amz-grant-* on uploads behave like AWS's, including on presigned URLs; clear InvalidRequest / AccessControlListNotSupported errors.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.what: preparePutObjectACL runs before the object bytes are stored. It reads the canned ACL and x-amz-grant-* values from headers AND (for SigV4 presigned URLs) the query string, where presigners hoist signed headers; it rejects conflicting duplicates, requires s3:PutObjectAcl for any explicit ACL, applies the bucket's ownership mode (BucketOwnerEnforced only accepts private / bucket-owner-full-control and makes the bucket owner the owner), always grants the owner FULL_CONTROL on custom grants, and stashes the resulting owner/grant Extended attributes in the request context. applyPutObjectACL copies them onto the new entry. putObjectACLPolicyRequest builds a cloned request whose ACL headers carry the effective (query-hoisted, normalized) values so bucket-policy conditions such as s3:x-amz-acl evaluate the ACL the object will actually get, keeping the original values for s3:x-amz-grant-* conditions.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.when: PutObject (regular and directory-marker paths), CreateMultipartUpload and other upload paths that call preparePutObjectACL before writing; putObjectACLPolicyRequest from iam.Auth (authRequestWithAuthType) and checkPolicyWithEntry.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.why: Consequence: without this, a presigned URL could set an ACL through the query string that policy evaluation never saw (bypassing a 'Deny unless x-amz-acl=private' policy), or ACLs would be accepted on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets where AWS rejects them. Design: the ACL is computed once, before the upload, so a rejected ACL fails fast instead of after the body was stored; the context key cannot be set by clients. AWS compatibility: AccessControlListNotSupported for disallowed ACLs on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets; SigV2 requests ignore query-borne ACL values; canned and grant headers are mutually exclusive.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.character: S3ApiServer methods that build ObjectTransaction mutations for versioned writes and deletes on the key's owner filer (the routed counterpart of the gateway-side pointer updates in s3api_object_versioning.go)
gotchas: objectWriteOwner here and routableWriteOwner in s3api_object_routed_write.go both resolve the owner from the same route key; keep them in sync.
routedDeleteNullVersion falls back to the lock path on any transport or transaction error (deletes are idempotent), while routedDeleteSpecificVersion fails the request instead.
routedMultipartFinalize keeps a gateway-side upload-exists check for older filers that ignore the mutation's condition.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.if_broken: Latest pointers drift from the actual newest version, locked versions get deleted, or completed uploads leave their staging directories behind.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.ux: Read-after-write correct 'latest' in multi-filer clusters; AccessDenied when a versioned delete hits a locked version.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.what: latestPointerRecompute builds a RECOMPUTE_LATEST mutation: the filer scans <key>.versions/ (descending or ascending by version-id format), writes the winner's file name, size and mtime plus copies of its version id / ETag / owner / delete-marker / storage class onto the .versions entry, and optionally stamps NoncurrentSinceNs on the demoted version. On top of it: routedVersionedFinalize (delete markers), routedMultipartFinalize (PUT the version file + delete the upload dir + recompute, guarded by an upload-exists precondition), routedDeleteSpecificVersion (recompute only if the deleted file was current, then delete, under a WORM condition), routedDeleteNullVersion, versionedFinalize (a putFinalize that rides inside putToFiler's transaction, with an off-ring afterCreate fallback), finalizeSuspendedNullWrite, and wormDeleteCondition (legal hold not ON AND retention-until elapsed; with bypass, the retention clause is gated to COMPLIANCE only).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.when: Versioned PutObject / CopyObject (via putToFiler's finalize), CompleteMultipartUpload on versioned buckets, versioned DeleteObject with or without versionId, delete-marker creation, suspended-versioning null writes, whenever objectWriteOwner/routableWriteOwner returns an owner.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.why: Consequence: with a filer ring, these transactions are what keep the version file and the latest pointer consistent; without atomicity a crash or a concurrent writer leaves latest pointing at a missing or older version. Design: putting the version PUT, the pointer recompute and (for multipart) the upload-dir removal in ONE transaction under the object path lock means readers never see a half-finalized version; WORM conditions are evaluated by the filer under that same lock, so a retention set concurrently cannot be raced past. The off-ring path keeps the older lock-and-update behavior. AWS compatibility: governance bypass lifts only GOVERNANCE retention, never COMPLIANCE or legal hold.
